conventions.convention: Y and the bounded physical domain are the unit cube; a is a measurable real scalar coefficient, periodic almost everywhere on the integer lattice, with 0 < λ ≤ a ≤ Λ. Coefficients are almost-everywhere classes, and affine sampling preserves these classes. Countable Choice is assumed.
H1-periodic is the H1 closure of smooth periodic functions; V-periodic is its zero-cell-mean subspace. Periodicity is a closure condition, not an imposed pointwise trace convention.
The corrector sign is p + gradient χ_p, and its additive constant is fixed by zero mean.
Underlying library coordinates start at zero; PDE labels i = 1,…,d denote library coordinate i−1. A* is defined by columns as the cell-averaged corrector flux.
Two-scale convergence uses positive scales tending to zero and finite sums of compactly supported smooth slow factors times smooth periodic fast factors.

FE-HMM is two-dimensional, with admissible NVB P1 macro meshes, periodic mean-zero P1 micro spaces, exact integral entries and exact real arithmetic. A micro square has lower corner x_K, the macro barycenter, and b_K(y) = a(x_K/ε + (δ/ε)y). Empty micro and macro bases are handled explicitly.
The cutoff corrector rate assumes u_0 belongs to C2 of the closed cube and H1-zero; it applies for 0 < ε ≤ 1/4 and uses a boundary cutoff transitioning between distances ε and 2ε.

Micro error compares the discrete tensor with the full periodic-coupling sampled tensor; resonance compares that sampled tensor with A*. Integer sampling ratios remove only resonance. The displayed perturbation estimate assumes Δ_micro + Δ_res < λ.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated scalar periodic ellipticity and mean-zero periodic-space hypotheses, each p ∈ R^d has a unique cell solution χ_p; p ↦ χ_p is linear, with gradient norm at most (Λ/λ)|p| and L2 norm at most √d(Λ/λ)|p|.
Every v ∈ V-periodic satisfies ||v||_L2 ≤ √d ||gradient v||_L2; every periodic H1 function has zero mean gradient. The gradient norm on V-periodic is complete and equivalent to its inherited H1 norm.

For periodic g ∈ L1(Y) and φ ∈ C1_c(Q), the integral of φ(x)g(x/ε) tends to the product of their integrals. For g ∈ L2(Y), its rescalings are uniformly L2-bounded for 0 < ε ≤ 1 and converge weakly to its cell mean.
Assuming Countable Choice, H1_0((0,1)^d; R) is a separable real Hilbert space, satisfies ||v||_L2 ≤ ||∂_0 v||_L2 ≤ ||gradient v||_L2, and every bounded sequence has an L2-convergent subsequence.

A bounded H1-zero sequence on the unit cube, along scales tending to zero, has a subsequence weakly converging in H1-zero and strongly in L2 to u, whose gradients two-scale converge to gradient_x u + gradient_y u_1 for u_1 ∈ L2(Q; V-periodic).
Under the scalar periodic ellipticity hypotheses, A* is symmetric and λ|p|² ≤ p·A*p ≤ Λ|p|² for every p ∈ R^d.

Every sampled coefficient retains λ ≤ b_K ≤ Λ; the full and finite periodic cell problems have unique solutions, their tensors are symmetric with λI ≤ A_K ≤ ΛI, and the macro system has a unique solution. The algorithm's exact elimination calls terminate without the singular-system branch and return the assembled variational solutions.

For the full and discrete cell solutions using the same sampled coefficient, p·(A_K^h−A_K^ex)p equals the squared coefficient-weighted gradient error. That error is bounded by every micro-space approximation error, and ||A_K^h−A_K^ex||_op ≤ η_K².

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 says, “The inherited H1 norm is complete because V-periodic is closed in H1-periodic.” This also requires completeness of the ambient H1 space. The published supplier lem-w-one-two-is-a-hilbert-space supplies precisely that fact, but it is absent from this item's deps and facts. The conclusion is valid; the omitted completeness prerequisite is immediately supplied by that lemma.

Step 1.1 explains its first equality p·A*q = integral a(p+gradient χ_p)·(q+gradient χ_q) as “adding the zero term with gradient χ_q.” Starting from p·A*q, the added term is integral a(q+gradient χ_q)·gradient χ_p, which vanishes by the q cell equation. Both cell equations were correctly established immediately beforehand, so the displayed identity and theorem remain valid; the explanation names the wrong corrector.
